props.title: Agentic Engineering
props.sub: the acting mind — AI agents that retrieve, reason, and act on the graph

props.foot: The graph is the agent's memory, its senses, and its list of safe things to do.

props.title: How the agent stays factual and remembers

cards.head: GraphRAG retrieval
cards.body: Pull the exact connected subgraph the question needs — that 86%-vs-32% edge from part two.

cards.head: Persistent memory
cards.body: Tools like cognee give the agent a graph-shaped memory across sessions — not a goldfish.

cards.head: Typed actions
cards.body: It can only call the operations the ontology allows — open a work item, page an owner.

props.foot: Grounded retrieval + durable memory + a safe action menu — the anti-hallucination kit.

props.title: The real skill: what you put in front of the model

cards.head: The subgraph
cards.body: Retrieve the small, relevant slice of the graph — not the whole thing, not random text.

cards.head: The schema
cards.body: Give the model the ontology so it grounds its terms and writes valid queries.

cards.head: Tools & memory
cards.body: Expose exactly the right MCP tools and recall past context — no more, no less.

props.foot: Prompt engineering grew up into context engineering — and the graph is your best context source.

props.title: Pinpoint questions and big-picture questions need different retrieval

right.head: Global (community) search
rows: Best for ‘what are our top risks?’

props.foot: Local for a pinpoint question, global for the big picture — serious systems ship both.
Creativity from the model, guarantees from the graph — together, that's trustworthy AI.

props.title: Three loops worth knowing by name

cards.head: ReAct
cards.body: Reason, then act with a tool, then observe — and repeat. The workhorse loop.

cards.head: Plan-and-execute
cards.body: Draft a full plan first, then run the steps — better for complex, multi-tool tasks.

cards.head: Reflection
cards.body: The agent critiques its own output and retries — catching mistakes before you see them.

props.foot: LangGraph makes all three explicit as graphs of steps — pick the shape per task.

props.title: Split the work when a single prompt gets overloaded

cards.head: Planner
cards.body: Breaks the question into steps — retrieve, correlate, decide — and delegates each.

cards.head: Specialists
cards.body: A graph-query agent, a log agent, an action agent — each an expert at exactly one tool.

cards.head: Orchestrator
cards.body: LangGraph wires them with loops and checks, so the team retries and revises instead of failing.

props.foot: Start with one agent. Split into a team only when a single prompt is doing too much.

props.title: The frameworks you'll actually wire together
props.foot: Retrieval + control flow + tools + memory — composed, not a single magic box.

props.title: Every source becomes a typed, permissioned tool
props.foot: MCP standardizes tools, so one agent reaches every source through typed, permissioned connectors.

props.title: An agent you can't evaluate or audit isn't production-ready

cards.head: Eval sets
cards.body: Known incidents with known root causes — measure the agent's F1 like a model, on every change.

cards.head: Human-in-the-loop
cards.body: Read-only actions auto-run; risky writes wait for one click of human approval.

cards.head: Full audit trail
cards.body: Every hop and action is logged on the graph — you can always ask ‘why did it do that?’

props.foot: The great demo is easy. Evaluation, approval gates, and audit are what make it shippable.
